sources.entry: difflib - (Python standard library) Helpers for computing deltas.

summary.name: difflib
summary.one_liner: Python standard library module for comparing sequences (mainly lists of text lines) and producing diffs in formats such as context, unified, HTML and ndiff-style deltas.
use_cases: Comparing two versions of a text or source file
Generating unified or context diffs for patches
Finding close matches for a misspelled word
Computing a similarity score between two strings
Showing intraline character changes in a diff
summary.what_it_does: The module compares sequences, mostly lists of text lines or file objects, and reports the differences. It can output unified diffs and context diffs in the style of diff and git diff, plus HTML tables with inter-line and intra-line highlights. The Differ and ndiff classes produce human-readable line-prefixed deltas with "?" guide lines for character-level changes. SequenceMatcher finds matching blocks, opcodes and a similarity ratio for any sequence of hashable elements, and get_close_matches returns the best approximate matches from a list of candidates.
notable: Ships with the Python standard library, no extra install needed
HTML side-by-side diff output via HtmlDiff
SequenceMatcher works on any hashable sequence, not just text
diff_bytes handles data with unknown or inconsistent encodings
caveats: The default autojunk heuristic is asymmetric and can give different results when inputs are swapped or cause large results on some data; it can be disabled or tuned
Differ-generated deltas are not minimal diffs
The HtmlDiff trailing newlines are stripped, so output can be incomplete (gh-71896)
